chapter: New York with Lester Young and Coleman Hawkins
title: Learning authentic boogie-woogie; Albert Ammons' son Gene
summary: Through Johnson and Ammons he learned the authentic boogie style, and Ammons spoke of his son Gene Ammons, whom Thompson later heard.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: And in fact it was through their friendship that I learned how to play the authentic boogie-woogie style of playing, which you know --
Pete Johnson and Albert Ammons, yes.

And naturally in the process I heard Albert talk about this son of his who he expected to be a great jazz tenor player, and I didn't even know where he was, I hadn't heard of him before. And then I looked up several years later and I found out what he was talking about, because his son turned out to be one of the finest jazz players in the world, Gene Ammons.
And he started playing with bands like Woody Herman and was featured as a great player. He was -- his father was right.
